text:
ana: Sync: quick runthrough of the "plumbing" for onprem networking edge cases (VPC peering, NAT fallback, customer IP preservation). Need launch must-have list + SLA tradeoffs. Who's in? :wave:

devon: I'm in. can we map the top 3 customer asks from last quarter?

ana: From notes: 1) preserve customer IPs for NATted clusters 2) automatic BGP fallback for DC outages 3) zero-touch peering for managed ISPs

sam.k: quick question — are we committing to deterministic failover <100ms? that will change the routing-agent design and testing matrix.

irene: i'd recommend two launch tiers: "MVP" (no BGP auto-swap, manual failover + clear operator steps) and "Tier1" (auto BGP, backed by SLA).

matt: MVP checklist (draft): - config flag to enable IP-preserve - operator opt-in flow - sample manifest in docs: `kubectl apply -f redwood-vpc-preserve.yaml` - simple e2e: bring down primary AZ and validate traffic path

sam.k: metrics we need: p95 connect-time, failover-time, and duplicate-route-count. propose SLOs: p95 failover < 500ms for Tier1, < 2s for MVP.

ana: agreed. also need a safe rollback path: if BGP auto-swap causes loops, immediate revert to customer-managed routing + notify net-ops. Add explicit revert play in runbook.

deploy-bot: DEPLOY STARTED: net-agent v0.3.2 -> staging (sha: abc123) :rocket:

devon: can eng-runtime/eng-ml weigh in on assumptions? e.g., the batcher tends to colocate requests; cross-subnet failover could spike egress and change cost dynamics.

irene: add an "egress-cost-estimate" step to the launch docs and a UI warning for private deployments that enable auto-routing. customers need visibility.

matt: action items: ana — consolidate requirements doc by Fri; devon — build cost model; sam.k — schedule SLO experiment; irene — draft runbook revert steps. i'll open a checklist PR and add reviewers.

ana: thanks all — i'll slot a 30m sync on Thu to finalize acceptance criteria. please drop short notes in the doc if you can't make it. :memo:
